Archie The desktop app

Install Archie.

Archie runs on your own computer. It isn’t a website you log into. Download it, open it, and your agent lives on your computer. Archie hasn’t shipped yet (here’s where it stands), so read this page as a preview: join the waitlist and this is where we’ll send you on release day. Below is where each platform’s download will live, and an honest account of what you’ll see the first time you open it.

Mac

macOS 12 Monterey or later. One download works on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

Download for Mac

Signed and notarized with Apple. It opens the way any other app does: no warnings, nothing to click past.

Windows

Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.

Download for Windows

Windows will try to stop you the first time. That’s expected with our first releases, and the next section explains exactly why; please read it before you install.

Windows

“Windows protected your PC”

When you open the installer, Windows will show a blue box with that heading, and the only obvious button will say Don’t run. Nothing is wrong. Here is how to get past it, and then why it happens at all, because you shouldn’t click through a security warning just because someone told you to.

1

Click “More info”

It’s the small link in the blue box, above the buttons. It’s easy to miss; it doesn’t look like a link.

2

Check the publisher

2 lines appear. The app name should read Archie. If it says anything else, stop. You don’t have our installer.

3

Click “Run anyway”

A new button appears once you’ve expanded More info. Archie installs normally from there, and you won’t see this screen again on this computer.

Why Windows says that

Windows trusts an app when its maker has bought a code-signing certificate, and it charges for that trust. The warning isn’t Windows detecting anything in Archie. It’s Windows telling you, accurately, that it doesn’t yet recognize who made it.

We’re a small team, and that certificate is on the list for when we’re further along. Until we buy it, every Windows build we ship shows this screen. We’d rather tell you that plainly than dress it up.

How to check us, not trust us

You don’t have to take our word for it. The download link on this page points at our public releases page on GitHub, where you can see every build we’ve ever published, when it went out, and how many people have downloaded it.

On the Mac we do hold Apple’s developer certificate, and that build is signed and notarized: the same team, the same code, checked by Apple. If you have both computers, install the Mac one first and see for yourself.

Yours alone

Your keys never reach us.

Archie asks for an AI key so your agent can think. It belongs to you, on an account you own and pay, and it lives in your operating system’s own vault: your Mac’s Keychain, or Windows Credential Manager. We have no way to read it.

What stays on your computer

  • Your AI keys and connected accounts
  • Your agent, its instructions, and its memory
  • Your files, notes, and knowledge base
  • Every message you and your agent exchange

What Otian’s servers hold

  • Your email address, so you can sign in
  • Whether you have a current plan
  • Which paid add-ons you’ve bought
  • Which version of Archie you are running
  • The messages to your phone, sealed, if you turn phone access on
  • Never your chats, files, or accounts

Once your key is in, your agent talks to the AI directly and your conversations never pass through us. Before it is, you are on the free credits, which we pay for, so those messages do pass through our server. We hold no copy on either path.

There is no analytics or tracking in Archie. If it crashes it writes a log and sends us the tail next time you open the app, so we learn something broke. You can switch that off under Account, and the log stays on your computer either way.

Stuck?

We’ll walk you through it.

Whenever you install Archie, you’ll be one of its first users, and we’d genuinely rather hear from you than have you give up quietly. If anything here doesn’t match what you’re seeing, tell us and we’ll get on a call.
